label: def:down-quark
title: Down quark
html:
The down quark is an unknot localized in a color tube with negative crossing orientation within the Borromean link \mathcal{B}_3.

  \mathfrak{d} =  \nu \big|_{\mathcal{B}_3, -}

The down quark differs from the up quark only by crossing orientation. At each crossing point within \mathcal{B}_3, the down quark strand passes under where the up quark passes over. This reversal contributes q^{-1} instead of q to the Skein polynomial.

Note (charge). The reversal is an exact mirror: the two orientations differ by a sign. The Coulomb charge is odd under that mirror, so the mechanism gives Q(\mathfrak{d}) = -Q(\mathfrak{u}) — equal magnitude, opposite sign — for every crossing count. It does not give -\tfrac{1}{3} against +\tfrac{2}{3}, whose ratio is -2; nor can it give thirds at all, since Q \in \tfrac{1}{2}\mathbb{Z}. The sharper consequence is that a mirror-odd charge makes the neutron the proton's exact opposite, Q(\mathfrak{n}) = -Q(\mathfrak{p}), so demanding a neutral neutron forces every quark charge to vanish. The Standard Model assignment escapes this only because it takes |Q_{\mathfrak{u}}| = 2|Q_{\mathfrak{d}}|, an asymmetry between the two orientations that a pure mirror cannot supply.
